title: SpaceX Crew Dragon

sources.title: Dragon astronauts name their spacecraft Endeavour, complete first manual flight test (Spaceflight Now)
Space as a Service: NASA and SpaceX find a new way of putting people into orbit (Nextgov)
JoyPro cockpit catalog (panels, items and grip functions of the variant)

intro: Crew Dragon is SpaceX's crew capsule, flying astronauts to the International Space Station since 2020. Instead of hand controllers and hundreds of switches it has three large touchscreens; the flight is automatic, and manual turning and moving commands are given with on-screen buttons. A few physical buttons below the screens back up the most critical commands. The labels of physical buttons other than the three listed are not public.

panels.name: Three flight displays
panels.text: Three large touchscreens hanging from the panel in front of the commander and the pilot.
panels.context: The crew works them with gloves that can touch screens; the flight itself is automatic.

controls.name: Left display
controls.text: The left touchscreen. It shows flight, system and camera pages.
controls.context: The crew picks the page by touch.

controls.name: Centre display
controls.text: The middle touchscreen. It shows flight and system pages.
controls.context: Both crew members can see and reach it.

controls.name: Right display
controls.text: The right touchscreen. It shows system and camera pages.
controls.context: The pilot on the right works it while the commander watches the left one.

panels.name: Physical button panel
panels.text: A row of real, guarded buttons below the screens for the most critical commands.
panels.context: They work even if the touchscreens fail; covers stop them from being pressed by accident.

controls.name: Emergency deorbit button
controls.text: Pressing this guarded button starts the emergency return to Earth: the capsule fires its engines to slow down and fall out of orbit (deorbit).
controls.context: It is for an emergency, for example a cabin problem that forces the crew home at once.

controls.name: Fire suppression button
controls.text: Pressing this button sets off the cabin's fire suppression.
controls.context: A fire in a closed capsule is very dangerous, so this command has its own physical button.

controls.name: Parachute deploy button
controls.text: Pressing this button lets out the parachutes.
controls.context: Normally the parachutes open automatically during the return; the button is the backup.

panels.name: Crew seats
panels.text: The seats of the crew, the commander and pilot in front of the screens.
panels.context: NASA flights carry up to four astronauts.

controls.name: Commander and pilot seats
controls.text: The two seats facing the screens, for the commander and the pilot.
controls.context: From these seats the crew monitors the flight and can take manual control on the screens.

controls.name: Mission specialist seats
controls.text: Two further seats for mission specialists, crew members who do not fly the capsule.
controls.context: They work on the space station once there.

areas.name: Touch flight controls
areas.text: The on-screen controls JoyPro lists as grips.

panels.name: Rotation controls (touchscreen)
panels.text: On-screen buttons for turning the capsule.
panels.context: Crew Dragon has no physical hand controllers; manual commands are given on the touchscreens.

controls.name: Rotation controls (touchscreen)
controls.text: On-screen buttons on the flight displays that turn the capsule: pitch, roll and yaw. Each touch fires the steering jets.
controls.context: On the first crewed flight in 2020, Bob Behnken and Doug Hurley flew the capsule by hand this way as a test.

panels.name: Translation controls (touchscreen)
panels.text: On-screen buttons for moving the capsule.
panels.context: They sit next to the docking camera picture, so the crew sees the effect at once.

controls.name: Translation controls (touchscreen)
controls.text: On-screen buttons next to the docking camera view that move the capsule forward, back, left, right, up and down without turning it.
controls.context: Docking is normally automatic; the buttons let the crew fly the approach by hand if needed.
